strengths: Humble verb itadaku and gochisōsama pairing are standard usage.
Visitor-not-required is correctly not presented as law.
Curriculum language “varies by school and era” is an honest hedge in the same paragraph as the weaker claim.
verified: Itadakimasu is a common pre-meal phrase; itadaku is a humble verb of receiving.
Group itadakimasu is common in many elementary school lunches.
Gochisōsama deshita is the common closer.
questionable: “Postwar school lunch, in many districts, standardized a group start” as the main historical cause of adult usage.
The word’s history “brushes against Buddhist vocabulary” (directionally fair, too vague to verify as stated).
needs_source: Any claim that postwar kyūshoku created or legally standardized itadakimasu.

issues.location: Not a Church Prayer — “Postwar school lunch… standardized a group start.”
issues.problem: The phrase and humble verb are older than postwar kyūshoku. School lunch spread the group recitation; it did not invent the table word. Stating standardization as origin overclaims.
issues.suggestion: Hedge: many adults learned a group start in the cafeteria; that explains volume better than an unbroken ancient law. Do not say postwar lunch standardized the phrase.
